- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.7) or shows sharp reversal, model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- If model shows strong upward spike (e.g., >10% above recent mean) with no recent negative sentiment, it often overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 30–50% in 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), model tends to lag behind true price; add 1–2 days of lag correction (forecast = true outcome - 1–2 days lag).
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 10–15 days, especially if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum but model forecasts decline, reverse direction by 1–2% for next 3–5 days unless confirmed by technical indicators.
